quote: C. M. Newman proved in 1976 the existence of a constant (now named after both mathematicians) for which the function has only real zeros if and only if the parameter exceeds that constant; Newman also conjectured properties about the constant
note: Newman's 1976 paper 'Fourier Transforms with only Real Zeros' (Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society, vol. 61, pp. 245-251) established the existence of the de Bruijn-Newman constant and posed the problem of determining its value through Newman's conjecture that it is non-negative. The problem of finding the exact value remains open.
